subject: maths
title: Angles in a Circle and Cyclic Quadrilaterals
meta: Lesson practice set · Question types of the April 2026 NIOS paper
instructions: Practice set for this lesson in the question types of the April 2026 paper.
Every answer shows the working. Where a question has OR, answer either one.
Questions from previous NIOS papers show the exam they appeared in.

questions.q: Angles in the same segment of a circle are —
questions.work: By the theorem, every angle subtended by the same arc in the same segment equals half the central angle, so they are all equal.

questions.q: An arc subtends x° at the centre and y° at a point on the remaining part of the circle. Then —
questions.work: The angle at the centre is double the angle on the circle: x = 2y.

questions.q: The angle in a semicircle is —
questions.work: The diameter subtends 180° at the centre, so it subtends 180°/2 = 90° at any point on the circle.

questions.q: For a cyclic quadrilateral, which is true?
options: One opposite angle is always obtuse
questions.work: Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral add up to 180° — they are supplementary.

questions.q: In a circle with centre O, ∠ABC = 100° and ∠BDC = 45° (A, B, C, D on the circle, ∠BAC and ∠BDC on the same arc BC). Then ∠ACB is —
Which of the following is always a cyclic quadrilateral?
questions.work: A quadrilateral is cyclic when opposite angles are supplementary. In a rectangle each angle is 90°, so 90° + 90° = 180° ✓. A general parallelogram or rhombus does not satisfy this.

questions.q: AOB is a diameter of a circle with centre O. If AC = 3 cm and BC = 4 cm (C on the circle), the radius is —
questions.work:
∠ACB = 90° (angle in a semicircle).
AB² = 3² + 4² = 25 ⇒ AB = 5 cm (diameter). Radius = 2.5 cm.

questions.q: AB is a diameter of a circle with centre O and ∠AOC = 120°. If D is on the circle on the other side of AB, then ∠BDC is —
In a cyclic quadrilateral ABCD, ∠A = 110°. Then ∠C is —
A chord of a circle equals its radius. The angle it subtends at a point on the major arc is —
questions.work:
The chord and two radii form an equilateral triangle, so the central angle is 60°.
Angle on the major arc = ½ × 60° = 30°.

sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark (fill in the blanks, match the columns or true/false).

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (i) In cyclic quadrilateral ABCD, ∠DAB = 110°, so ∠BCD = ____. (ii) AB is a chord of a circle with centre O, ∠OAB = 40° and C is on the major arc; ∠ACB = ____.
questions.answer:
(i) Opposite angles are supplementary: 180° − 110° = 70°.
(ii) OA = OB, so ∠OBA = 40° and ∠AOB = 180° − 80° = 100°; ∠ACB = ½ × 100° = 50°.

questions.q: Write True or False: (i) A chord equal to the radius subtends 30° at a point on the minor arc. (ii) ∠PAQ = 35° is inscribed in a circle with centre O standing on chord PQ; then ∠OPQ = 50°.
questions.answer:
(i) False: the central angle is 60°; on the major arc the angle is 30°, on the minor arc it is 180° − 30° = 150°.
(ii) False: ∠POQ = 2 × 35° = 70°; OP = OQ, so ∠OPQ = (180° − 70°)/2 = 55°.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (i) In cyclic quadrilateral PQRS, side PS is produced to A and ∠PQR = 80°; ∠ASR = ____. (ii) If ∠R = 78°, then ∠P = ____.
questions.answer:
(i) An exterior angle of a cyclic quadrilateral equals the interior opposite angle: ∠ASR = ∠PQR = 80°. (Also ∠PSR = 100°, so ∠ASR = 180° − 100° = 80°.)
(ii) ∠P + ∠R = 180° ⇒ ∠P = 102°.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (i) In cyclic quadrilateral ABCD, ∠DBC = 55° and ∠BAC = 45°; then ∠BCD = ____. (ii) The angle subtended at the centre by a semicircle is a ____ angle.

sections.passage: A Ferris wheel is a circle with centre O. Cabins A, B, C and D are on the wheel. The arc AB subtends ∠AOB = 140° at the centre. C is on the major arc AB and D is on the minor arc AB, so ACBD is a cyclic quadrilateral.

questions.q: Find the angle subtended by a chord equal to the radius of a circle at a point in the major segment.
questions.answer:
Join the chord's ends A and B to the centre O. OA = OB = AB, so △OAB is equilateral and ∠AOB = 60°.
Angle at a point C in the major segment = ½∠AOB = 30°.

questions.q: ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral with ∠A = (2x + 4)°, ∠B = (y + 3)°, ∠C = (2y + 10)° and ∠D = (4x − 5)°. Find x and y.
questions.note: April 2025 asked the same type of question with its own expressions for the angles.

questions.q: O is the centre of a circle, ∠SOQ = 150° and P, R are on the circle so that PQRS is cyclic with P on the minor arc QS. Find x = ∠SRQ and y = ∠SPQ.
questions.answer:
x = ½∠SOQ = ½ × 150° = 75° (angle on the major arc).
PQRS is cyclic: y = 180° − x = 105°.

questions.q: In a circle with centre O, ∠BAC = 35°. Find ∠OBC.
Find the measure of ∠ABC if the minor arc ABC subtends 120° at the centre O (B on the minor arc).
questions.answer:
The arc AC not containing B subtends the reflex angle 360° − 120° = 240° at O.
∠ABC = ½ × 240° = 120°.

questions.q: O is the centre of a circle and A, B, C lie on it with ∠AOC = 120°. Find ∠ABC when B is on the major arc.
Prove that angles in the same segment of a circle are equal.
questions.answer:
Given: a circle with centre O; ∠ACB and ∠ADB are in the same segment, standing on arc AB.
To prove: ∠ACB = ∠ADB.
Construction: join OA and OB.
Proof: the angle subtended by an arc at the centre is double the angle subtended at any point on the remaining circle.
So ∠AOB = 2∠ACB and ∠AOB = 2∠ADB.
Hence 2∠ACB = 2∠ADB, i.e. ∠ACB = ∠ADB. Proved.

questions.q: Prove that the opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral are supplementary.
questions.answer:
Given: ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral, centre O.
To prove: ∠A + ∠C = 180° and ∠B + ∠D = 180°.
Construction: join OB and OD.
Proof: arc BCD subtends ∠BOD (marked x) at the centre and ∠BAD on the circle, so ∠BAD = ½x.
Arc BAD subtends the reflex angle (360° − x) at the centre and ∠BCD on the circle, so ∠BCD = ½(360° − x).
Adding: ∠A + ∠C = ½x + 180° − ½x = 180°.
Since the angles of a quadrilateral add to 360°, ∠B + ∠D = 360° − 180° = 180°. Proved.

questions.q: ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral in which AB is a diameter and ∠ADC = 130°. Find ∠BAC.
questions.answer:
∠ABC = 180° − ∠ADC = 50° (opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral).
∠ACB = 90° (angle in a semicircle).
In △ABC: ∠BAC = 180° − 90° − 50° = 40°.

questions.q: Prove that the angle subtended by an arc at the centre of a circle is double the angle subtended by it at any point on the remaining part of the circle.
questions.answer:
Given: arc AB of a circle with centre O; C is a point on the remaining part.
To prove: ∠AOB = 2∠ACB.
Construction: join CO and produce it to a point D.
Proof: in △OAC, OA = OC (radii), so ∠OAC = ∠OCA.
The exterior angle ∠AOD = ∠OAC + ∠OCA = 2∠OCA …(1)
Similarly in △OBC, ∠BOD = 2∠OCB …(2)
Adding (1) and (2): ∠AOD + ∠BOD = 2(∠OCA + ∠OCB), i.e. ∠AOB = 2∠ACB. Proved.
(For a major arc, the same steps give reflex ∠AOB = 2∠ACB.)

questions.q: Two circles intersect at A and B. AC and AD are diameters of the two circles. Prove that C, B and D are collinear.
questions.answer:
Join AB, BC and BD.
AC is a diameter of the first circle, so ∠ABC = 90° (angle in a semicircle).
AD is a diameter of the second circle, so ∠ABD = 90°.
∠ABC + ∠ABD = 90° + 90° = 180°, so CBD is a straight line.
Hence C, B and D are collinear.
